title: Classification-driven interference attenuation: adaptive tenant throttles and progressive preemption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During mixed-tenant workloads on Dedicated clusters we observe intermittent tail-latency spikes caused by a small percentage of tenants that run very bursty or KV-cache-unfriendly workloads. Existing hard-quotas or static lane fencing lead to poor utilization or abrupt failures for tenants with legitimate short bursts. Goal: introduce a classification-driven attenuation layer that (1) identifies tenant workload signatures in real time, (2) applies progressive soft-throttles and adaptive preemption policies based on tenant class and risk score, and (3) provides transparent metrics and rollback controls for SRE/Customer success.
design_summary: We will build a lightweight per-tenant classifier in the routing plane that uses short-run features (QPS histogram, sequence-length distribution, cache-miss rate, kernel memory footprint, priority flag) to assign tenants to classes: steady, bursty-cache-friendly, bursty-cache-unfriendly, and latency-sensitive. For non-latency-sensitive but cache-unfriendly tenants we apply a three-stage attenuation: 1) smoothing via token-level pacing + smart batching window reduction; 2) probabilistic KV eviction hints + reduced batch concurrency; 3) progressive preemption to lower-priority nodes (with graceful fallback). The system exposes a safety net hard quota that is only triggered if all soft mitigations fail. Decisions are parameterized and stored in config with dynamic flags for fast rollback.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Trade-offs: classifier complexity vs. inference latency (we keep classifier inline but extremely lightweight). Risk of misclassification affecting latency-sensitive tenants — mitigated by conservative thresholds and fail-open defaults. Utilization may drop slightly for clusters with many adaptive preemptions; we will monitor unit-cost and SLOs and adjust scores. Requires modest routing-plane CPU and telemetry instrumentation.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: tenant_risk_score, tenant_class, soft_throttle_rate, kv_eviction_hint_rate, preemption_count, post-attenuation_p99_latency_by_tenant. Alerts: sustained preemption_count > 10/min for a tenant (investigate), cluster-level soft_throttle_rate > 20% for 5m (auto-escalate), and any latency-sensitive tenant p99 degraded > 15% relative to baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Lab experiments on staging clusters with recorded production traffic replay (2 weeks). 2) Canary: enable for 5 low-traffic dedicated pools for 1 week with metrics-only mode (no effect) then soft-throttle mode for another week. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of dedicated capacity over 3 weeks with monitoring dashboard and automated rollback. 4) Full launch gated on 0% increase in customer-impacting incidents and <5% unit-cost regression.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier precision >= 85% for bursty vs steady classes on replay dataset
Median p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants changes < 5% during canary
Soft throttles reduce tail latencies caused by cache-unfriendly tenants by >= 30% without triggering hard quotas
Dashboard surfaces tenant risk scores and per-tenant mitigation actions with <30s lag
implementation_notes: Implementation will touch routing-service (classifier + decision engine), serving-agent (apply pacing and KV hints), autoscaler (honor preemption signals), and console (new dashboards). Configs stored in config-store with rollout flags. Initial classifier is rule-based; follow-up iteration will replace with small ML model if needed.
